deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. Gauss reused a pre-printed French circular from the Imperial Academy of Sciences of St. Petersburg as scrap paper.

The header is handwritten: 'St.-Pétersbourg, ce 16/28 janvier 1850'. This is a double date, Julian 16 January = Gregorian 28 January 1850.

The printed text informs external members that the Academy, to keep closer and more regular contact with them, has decided to give each a free copy of its Bulletin. A sufficient number of copies, starting with the current volume, has been deposited with its commission agent, Léopold Voss, bookseller in Leipzig. By presenting the enclosed coupon, the recipient can collect his copy of the Bulletin physico-mathématique, vol. VIII and following, at that shop.

The circular is signed by the Secrétaire perpétuel. The signature is probably that of Paul Heinrich Fuss, permanent secretary 1826–1855. It carries the handwritten serial number 'No 83'.

Gauss added a note in his own hand: 'Der Bon an Voss abgeschickt 1850 Febr. 16.' This means 'the coupon sent to Voss, 16 Feb 1850'. It records that he redeemed the voucher.

The only computational content is implicit in the dual date. In 1850 the Julian calendar ran 12 days behind the Gregorian, and the dates given (16 vs 28) are consistent with that.

The neighbouring pages are a different matter. The previous page has a polar-form analysis of a complex equation and logarithmic numerical work. The next page has numerical tables and the address side of a 1842 Berlin Academy mailing. Neither has any mathematical connection to this sheet; they simply share the reused-paper context.

results.what: Administrative circular from the St. Petersburg Academy offering external members a free subscription to its Bulletin physico-mathématique (vol. VIII ff.) via the Leipzig bookseller Leopold Voss, with Gauss's note that he sent the coupon on 16 Feb 1850

deep.surprise_reason: The page has no mathematical content. It is a printed circular reused as scrap, with a dated administrative note by Gauss. It is of minor biographical interest only: it documents Gauss's receipt of the St. Petersburg Bulletin from 1850.

checkable.asserts: The dual date 16/28 January reflects the 12-day Julian–Gregorian offset valid between 1 March 1800 and 28 February 1900.
Standard formula for the Julian–Gregorian difference in days gives 12 for the year 1850, confirming the date pair.

transcription_corrections: Signature after 'Le Secrétaire perpétuel:' is most plausibly 'Fuss' (Paul Heinrich Fuss, permanent secretary 1826–1855); the flourished hand makes it hard to read, but the identification fits the date.
'rèsolu' (grave accent) is as printed in the original, a typographic slip for 'résolu'; 'a cet effet' likewise lacks the accent on 'à' in the print.
'No. 83.' is handwritten in the original (printed 'No' followed by handwritten '83').
Gauss's marginal note reads 'Der Bon an Voss abgeschickt / 1850 Febr. 16.' The transcription is correct.
